decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Arithmetic and Proportions

outcomes.description: Calculate with signed integers, fractions, and decimals.
Solve proportion, percentage, and unit-conversion problems.
Check calculations using bounds, scientific notation, and significant figures.

practice: Solve mixed problems and diagnose numerical errors.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebra and Functions

outcomes.description: Solve linear, quadratic, rational, and inequality problems with domain checks.
Translate formulas, graphs, tables, compositions, and inverse functions.
Solve exponential and logarithmic models and interpret parameters.
Calculate with Cartesian complex numbers and interpret conjugation and modulus.

excludes: Polar trigonometric form; calculus; abstract algebra

practice: Construct and check symbolic models.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Geometry and Trigonometry

outcomes.description: Solve Euclidean measurement problems using similarity, distance, and angle relations.
Derive unit-circle identities and use radians, sinusoids, and complex polar form.

practice: Solve geometric and periodic-model problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Sets, Logic, and Proof

outcomes.description: Translate quantified statements, implications, converses, and negations.
Use relations, functions, equivalence classes, and countability arguments.
Construct direct, contrapositive, contradiction, and counterexample arguments.
Prove recursive claims by ordinary and strong induction.

includes: Proof grammar and informal set foundations

practice: Write proofs and repair invalid arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Data Literacy

outcomes.description: Calculate and interpret location, spread, proportions, and standardized differences.
Choose plots revealing distributions, relationships, and misleading scales.
Create documented spreadsheets handling units, identifiers, and missing values.

practice: Clean and report a small dataset.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra

outcomes.description: Solve linear systems and interpret rank and nullity.
Determine bases, independence, coordinates, and orthogonal projections.
Represent real and complex linear maps under basis changes.
Compute eigenvalue and singular-value decompositions and justify applicability.

practice: Solve matrix problems with geometric explanations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus

outcomes.description: Evaluate limits and explain continuity graphically and numerically.
Differentiate compositions and solve rate and optimization problems.
Evaluate integrals and apply the fundamental theorem.
Test series convergence and bound Taylor approximation errors.

practice: Solve extended modeling and approximation problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus

outcomes.description: Compute gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, and local linearizations.
Evaluate multiple integrals with coordinate-change Jacobians.
Apply Green, Gauss, and Stokes theorems with their hypotheses.

includes: Curves, surfaces, derivatives, and field integrals

practice: Solve field problems in multiple coordinates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Discrete Mathematics

outcomes.description: Derive counts using bijections, inclusion-exclusion, and generating functions.
Prove connectivity and tree properties and construct graph models.
Solve recurrences and justify asymptotic growth bounds.

practice: Prove counts and analyze discrete constructions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Elementary Number Theory

outcomes.description: Prove factorization results using divisibility and Euclidean algorithms.
Solve modular equations using inverses, Euler's theorem, and CRT.
Prove solvability or impossibility of elementary Diophantine equations.

practice: Write proofs and work explicit modular calculations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability

outcomes.description: Construct joint and conditional laws and apply Bayes' rule.
Derive transformed discrete and continuous random-variable distributions.
Calculate moments, covariance, and elementary conditional expectations.
Derive concentration bounds and select LLN or CLT approximations.

includes: Sample spaces, independence, densities, and limit reasoning

practice: Compare exact distribution calculations with approximations.

decks.subject: mathematics

includes: Applied inference; fitting and spreadsheet procedures taught locally
excludes: General asymptotic proofs; causal identification theory

practice: Produce assumption-sensitive data analysis reports.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Equations and Dynamics

outcomes.description: Solve standard ODEs and check existence and uniqueness hypotheses.
Solve linear systems using eigenstructure and interpret phase portraits.
Analyze equilibria, local stability, and elementary bifurcations.

practice: Derive models and compare solutions with phase portraits.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Analysis

outcomes.description: Bound conditioning, truncation, and floating-point effects separately.
Implement direct and iterative solvers with residual diagnostics.

Implement ODE schemes and analyze consistency, stability, and convergence.

practice: Implement algorithms and measure error scaling.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis

Prove differentiation and Riemann-integration theorems and justify limit exchanges.

practice: Write proofs and construct hypothesis-sensitive counterexamples.

practiceNotes: This is a curriculum proposal for human review. Flashcards support retrieval and discrimination; proofs, programming, experiments, and research judgment require the extended practice specified.

Chemical, biological, and physical experiments require supervision, local risk assessment, facility procedures, and approved waste handling; none of these external conditions is represented as satisfied.

Radioactive sources, regulated biological materials, lasers, cryogens, and high-power equipment require facility-specific training and authorization. Supplied datasets and simulations offer alternatives.
Human-participant, animal, field-collection, and sensitive genomic work may require ethics approval, consent, permits, privacy safeguards, and data-use agreements.
Security exercises must use owned or explicitly authorized systems. Educational cryptographic implementations are not deployment recommendations.
Embedded and robotics practice should begin in simulation or supervised low-energy hardware. Educational success does not establish safety certification.
Drug-discovery, physiology, and epidemiology exercises do not authorize prescribing, clinical treatment, or operational public-health decisions.
Computational projects require suitable software and computing access; platform-specific installation and facility procedures should be selected during implementation.
